method: Google FLEURS first local test recording per language and six ESC-10 recordings in SHA-256(excerpt-v1/filename) order. Mono PCM 16 kHz. The target recording follows three seconds of speech from another language and precedes three more seconds from that speaker. Both surrounding excerpts are replaced for the second run. Playback pauses every 2.91 s. Rehear the target with its language hint through the saved turn, across pauses. Assert bit-identical PCM and identical speech responses for the two contexts. Character edit distance uses casefold, NFC and Unicode letter, mark and number categories.

blind_reader.method: For each target send a new reader the film times and the full speech-reader JSON, with no labels, waveform, picture or shell. Use the first released turn covering the target end. Before is the existing whole-turn request at 8797b31. Exact is the new excerpt request. Both use the same language hint and source, with the same three seconds of another speaker before and after. Run the 24 responses in a fixed shuffled order (seed 17422). A match is yes for FLEURS and no for ESC-10; unclear is an abstention. Quotes use the source language.
blind_reader.prompt_template: You checked the speech in a film. Answer just for {a} to {b} seconds on the film clock. Do you have evidence of a voice, and which words in that interval could you quote? Keep the recording's original language and wording. If no words are supported, leave the quote empty. Return a JSON object with voice (yes, no, or unclear) and quote (a string).
